name: layout-composition-resolution
body: Layout composition resolution: `{{ template "<name>" . }}` is the standard Go html/template action over the library's layout namespace, not one of the six layout helpers (template-language). Its name is the library layout's layer-relative forward-slash path — `slides/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a slide layout and `sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl` for a section layout. That name is the same string on Windows, macOS and Linux and wherever the layer sits on disk; it is the layout's path within its layer, not the template name, and it carries no layer root, `templates/` prefix, drive letter, backslash or absolute path. The namespace holds the layout texts of the layer it is built for, keyed by that layer-relative name and parsed with the executing template's own owning layer's function set: at render time it is the merged library's layout set, and at the load-time example check the external layer's namespace holds only that layer's own layouts while the local layer's namespace holds the merged set (example-layout-composition). A layout thus invokes another layout its namespace carries, a slide layout or a section layout alike, by that layer-relative name: a local-layer layout invokes an external-layer layout by the target's own layer-relative name (for example `{{ template "sections/<template-name>/layout.html.tmpl" . }}`), and an external-layer layout's `{{ template }}` call naming a local-layer layout is a templates error at the external layer's own load. A `{{ template }}`-invoked layout executes in the invoking template's own namespace, so its `media` helper binds to the invoking template's own owning layer; a `section` helper call is the composition that executes a target under the target's own owning layer (library-layer-references). A templates error reports the invoking layout's full on-disk file path and line; when the error concerns an unresolved `{{ template }}` target it also quotes the layout name exactly as the author wrote it. The on-disk path is display-only and is never accepted as a layout name.
